summary: Approved for the scoped valid-layout replay fix. Column-name and recorded-version boundaries discard the prior sample, rerun configuration, clear rendering state, reset header cadence, and restore or re-resolve sort state. The tables/indexes boundary matrix and description checks pass, race testing is clean, and a source mutation confirms the same-version tests are discriminating. No in-scope security blocker was found. The separately documented malformed-Ncols debt [020] remains reproducible and is neither fixed nor claimed closed by this diff.

findings.category: Untrusted deserialization / malformed archive bounds safety (existing debt [020])
findings.title: Dishonest Ncols still causes an index-out-of-range panic outside the valid-layout contract
findings.description: An attacker supplying a recorded archive can keep version, Cols, row widths, and Nrows consistent between two tables samples while declaring an excessive Ncols. PGresult.validate does not compare Ncols with len(Cols), so the new slices.Equal layout check does not identify a boundary. On the second sample, stat.diff allocates and iterates using the attacker-declared current width and indexes past the previous row, crashing report replay. This is the already registered [020] malformed-shape class; Task 04 explicitly limits Decision 9 to valid adjacent layouts and does not modify the shared parser or claim to close this debt.
findings.location: internal/stat/postgres.go:558-572,619-645 (pre-existing shared parser/diff); report/report.go:274 (layout comparison in the supplied diff)
findings.evidence: Generated a temporary synthetic two-tick tables tar whose rows and Cols were internally consistent but whose declared Ncols was excessive, then ran `go run ./cmd report -T -f <temporary-archive>` with a bounded time range. The command exited nonzero with a sanitized classification of runtime panic, index out of range, and a stack frame in internal/stat.diff. Source inspection confirms validate checks row width against Cols and Nrows against Values, but not Ncols against Cols. The temporary archive was deleted; no raw payload is included here.
findings.recommendation: Handle [020] in its separately scoped shared-validation change: reject negative or inconsistent Ncols/Nrows/Cols shapes at PGresult validation, including Ncols == len(Cols), and retain defensive index checks in diff/alignment consumers. Add malformed same-column-name replay tests that require a clean error rather than a panic. Do not represent Decision 9 or this Task 04 report as closing [020].

The instrumented mutant compiled and ran the named parent and all four same-version old-to-new leaves, exited 1, produced two first-new-layout-sample/no-diff assertion failures and two stale-width errors. state_and_sort_analysis.command: Traced readTar -> processData -> view.Configure -> stat.Compare/diff/sort -> formatStatSample/printStatSample for both boundary directions and requested stats_age ordering.
state_and_sort_analysis.result: prevStat, prevMeta, and prevTs are replaced before continue, preventing a cross-layout delta. On every version-or-Cols boundary, Aligned/Cols/ColsWidth and header cadence are reset, orderConfigured is re-armed, and the originally captured seed key/direction are restored before the next sample resolves -o by name. Existing PGresult.sort rejects a key outside the current first row. No stale sort index or old-layout value was observed in the valid-layout matrix.
